Finish the resolver in `src/`. `src/index.js` re-exports `ResolveError`, `parseVersion`, `compareVersions`, `parseRange`, `satisfies` and `maxSatisfying` from `src/semver.js` and `ConflictError` and `resolve` from `src/resolve.js`; keep that surface. `ResolveError` extends `Error`, sets `name` to `'ResolveError'`, carries a `code` and is constructed as `(code, message)`. A version is exactly three numeric parts with no leading zeros and no suffix; `parseVersion` returns `{ major, minor, patch }` and otherwise throws `'BAD_VERSION'` with message `invalid version: <text>`. `compareVersions(left, right)` returns -1, 0 or 1 by comparing the three parts numerically, so `1.10.0` is above `1.9.0`.

`parseRange(text)` turns a range into the list of comparators that must all hold, each `{ operator, version }` with an operator of `>=`, `<=`, `>`, `<` or `=`. Whitespace around the range is ignored and one or more spaces separate conjuncts. `*` alone means no comparators at all and may not appear beside anything else. A bare version, or one written with `=`, is an equality comparator. `^V` means at least `V` and below the next version that changes the leftmost non-zero part: `^1.2.3` spans up to but excluding `2.0.0`, `^0.2.3` up to `0.3.0`, and `^0.0.3` up to `0.0.4`. `~V` means at least `V` and below the next minor, so `~1.2.3` spans up to `1.3.0`. Anything else, including an empty range, a lone operator, an operator separated from its version by a space, or an unparseable version, throws `'BAD_RANGE'` with message `invalid range: <text>`. `satisfies(version, range)` tests one version against every comparator, and `maxSatisfying(versions, range)` returns the highest satisfying version of a list or null.

`resolve(registry, rootDeps)` picks exactly one version per package. The registry maps a package name to an object of versions, each version to metadata whose optional `deps` maps a package name to a range. It is validated up front: a non-object registry throws `'BAD_REGISTRY'` with message `registry must be an object`, a non-object package entry gives `registry entry must be an object: <name>`, every version key must parse, non-object metadata gives `metadata must be an object: <name>@<version>`, and a dependency map that is not an object throws `'BAD_DEPENDENCIES'` with message `dependencies of <name>@<version> must be an object`. The root map is validated the same way, with `root dependencies must be an object`, and every range in either place must parse.

Resolution keeps a list of constraints per package and a set of pending packages, seeded from the root dependencies taken in ascending name order, where each root constraint records the origin `<root>`. While anything is pending, take the lexicographically smallest pending name and select it: a name absent from the registry throws `'UNKNOWN_PACKAGE'` with message `unknown package: <name>`; otherwise the candidates are the registry's versions of that package that satisfy every constraint recorded for it so far, and the highest candidate wins. Selecting a package at a version gives it a chain, which is the origin recorded with its first constraint followed by ` > <name>@<version>`, so a root dependency `a` chosen at 1.0.0 has the chain `<root> > a@1.0.0`. Its dependencies are then walked in ascending name order: each adds a constraint whose origin is the selecting package's chain, and a dependency that has not been selected becomes pending, while one that is already selected must still satisfy the new range. A package with no satisfying candidate, and a selected package that a later constraint contradicts, both raise `ConflictError`, which extends `ResolveError`, sets `name` to `'ConflictError'` and `code` to `'CONFLICT'`, and carries `packageName`, `available` (that package's versions in ascending order) and `constraints`, the recorded constraints as `{ range, via }` in the order they arrived. Its message is `cannot satisfy <name>: ` followed by those constraints as `<range> (from <via>)` joined with `, `. On success the result is `{ resolved, order }`, where `resolved` maps names to versions in ascending name order and `order` lists the names in the order they were selected. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. The standard is `node --test test/*.test.js` passing in the workspace root.

header.system:
You are an AI agent powered by DeepSeek Harness.

You implement one program task in the workspace you are given, against its own test suite, and you stop when the tests pass.

The workspace is your working directory: every bash command and every file path resolves inside it, so read and edit its files by their relative paths and never search outside it.


Use the read tool — not shell commands like cat — to inspect text files. Results include line numbers. Use offset and limit to continue reading large files.

Use the write tool to create files or completely replace file contents. Existing files are overwritten, so read an existing file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it) and prefer edit for targeted changes.

Use the edit tool for targeted changes to existing UTF-8 text files. It replaces literal old_string with new_string; by default old_string must appear exactly once. If old_string appears multiple times, provide a more specific old_string or set replace_all to true. Read the file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it), unless you just created or edited it in this session.

Check the [exit code: N] marker on every bash result; investigate failures before moving on.

Track every background job id you start. You are notified in-session when a job finishes — do not busy-poll or sleep on one; keep working on independent steps and do not duplicate a running job's work. Before giving a final answer, collect every still-relevant job with job_output (set wait: true only when you are genuinely blocked on it), and job_kill jobs that stopped mattering.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend.

old_string.description: Literal text to replace. Must match exactly.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job by job id. Returns immediately; the job settles as killed once its work actually stops.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job. Stream jobs return only output since the previous read; final-output jobs return their result after settlement. Every response ends with `[status: ...]`. Reads are non-blocking unless `wait: true`, which waits up to the configured cap.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job reaches a terminal status or the timeout expires. A timed-out wait returns [status: running] and leaves the job alive.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds (only meaningful with wait: true). Defaults to the configured wait timeout; capped by the configured maximum.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

tools.name: skill
tools.description: Load the full instructions for an available skill. Call this with the exact skill name from the session skill catalog before acting on a task that names or clearly matches that skill.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

1: /**
2:  * A small semantic-version dialect: three numeric parts, and ranges built from
3:  * comparators, carets and tildes.
4:  *
5:  * Parsing and ordering of plain versions work; ranges do not exist yet.
6:  */
7: 
8: /** Error raised for malformed versions, ranges, registries and unsatisfiable graphs. */
9: export class ResolveError extends Error {
10:   /**
11:    * @param {string} code Stable machine-readable reason.
12:    * @param {string} message Human-readable detail.
13:    */
14:   constructor(code, message) {
15:     super(message);
16:     this.name = 'ResolveError';
17:     this.code = code;
18:   }
19: }
20: 
21: const VERSION_PATTERN = /^(0|[1-9]\d*)\.(0|[1-9]\d*)\.(0|[1-9]\d*)$/;
22: 
23: /**
24:  * Parse a version string.
25:  *
26:  * @param {string} text Version to parse.
27:  * @returns {{major: number, minor: number, patch: number}} Parsed parts.
28:  */
29: export function parseVersion(text) {
30:   const match = typeof text === 'string' ? VERSION_PATTERN.exec(text) : null;
31:   if (match === null) throw new ResolveError('BAD_VERSION', `invalid version: ${text}`);
32:   return { major: Number(match[1]), minor: Number(match[2]), patch: Number(match[3]) };
33: }
34: 
35: /**
36:  * Order two versions.
37:  *
38:  * @param {string} left First version.
39:  * @param {string} right Second version.
40:  * @returns {-1|0|1} Comparison result.
41:  */
42: export function compareVersions(left, right) {
43:   const a = parseVersion(left);
44:   const b = parseVersion(right);
45:   for (const part of ['major', 'minor', 'patch']) {
46:     if (a[part] !== b[part]) return a[part] < b[part] ? -1 : 1;
47:   }
48:   return 0;
49: }

goal.objective:
Finish the resolver in `src/`. `src/index.js` re-exports `ResolveError`, `parseVersion`, `compareVersions`, `parseRange`, `satisfies` and `maxSatisfying` from `src/semver.js` and `ConflictError` and `resolve` from `src/resolve.js`; keep that surface. `ResolveError` extends `Error`, sets `name` to `'ResolveError'`, carries a `code` and is constructed as `(code, message)`. A version is exactly three numeric parts with no leading zeros and no suffix; `parseVersion` returns `{ major, minor, patch }` and otherwise throws `'BAD_VERSION'` with message `invalid version: <text>`. `compareVersions(left, right)` returns -1, 0 or 1 by comparing the three parts numerically, so `1.10.0` is above `1.9.0`.

`parseRange(text)` turns a range into the list of comparators that must all hold, each `{ operator, version }` with an operator of `>=`, `<=`, `>`, `<` or `=`. Whitespace around the range is ignored and one or more spaces separate conjuncts. `*` alone means no comparators at all and may not appear beside anything else. A bare version, or one written with `=`, is an equality comparator. `^V` means at least `V` and below the next version that changes the leftmost non-zero part: `^1.2.3` spans up to but excluding `2.0.0`, `^0.2.3` up to `0.3.0`, and `^0.0.3` up to `0.0.4`. `~V` means at least `V` and below the next minor, so `~1.2.3` spans up to `1.3.0`. Anything else, including an empty range, a lone operator, an operator separated from its version by a space, or an unparseable version, throws `'BAD_RANGE'` with message `invalid range: <text>`. `satisfies(version, range)` tests one version against every comparator, and `maxSatisfying(versions, range)` returns the highest satisfying version of a list or null.

`resolve(registry, rootDeps)` picks exactly one version per package. The registry maps a package name to an object of versions, each version to metadata whose optional `deps` maps a package name to a range. It is validated up front: a non-object registry throws `'BAD_REGISTRY'` with message `registry must be an object`, a non-object package entry gives `registry entry must be an object: <name>`, every version key must parse, non-object metadata gives `metadata must be an object: <name>@<version>`, and a dependency map that is not an object throws `'BAD_DEPENDENCIES'` with message `dependencies of <name>@<version> must be an object`. The root map is validated the same way, with `root dependencies must be an object`, and every range in either place must parse.

Resolution keeps a list of constraints per package and a set of pending packages, seeded from the root dependencies taken in ascending name order, where each root constraint records the origin `<root>`. While anything is pending, take the lexicographically smallest pending name and select it: a name absent from the registry throws `'UNKNOWN_PACKAGE'` with message `unknown package: <name>`; otherwise the candidates are the registry's versions of that package that satisfy every constraint recorded for it so far, and the highest candidate wins. Selecting a package at a version gives it a chain, which is the origin recorded with its first constraint followed by ` > <name>@<version>`, so a root dependency `a` chosen at 1.0.0 has the chain `<root> > a@1.0.0`. Its dependencies are then walked in ascending name order: each adds a constraint whose origin is the selecting package's chain, and a dependency that has not been selected becomes pending, while one that is already selected must still satisfy the new range. A package with no satisfying candidate, and a selected package that a later constraint contradicts, both raise `ConflictError`, which extends `ResolveError`, sets `name` to `'ConflictError'` and `code` to `'CONFLICT'`, and carries `packageName`, `available` (that package's versions in ascending order) and `constraints`, the recorded constraints as `{ range, via }` in the order they arrived. Its message is `cannot satisfy <name>: ` followed by those constraints as `<range> (from <via>)` joined with `, `. On success the result is `{ resolved, order }`, where `resolved` maps names to versions in ascending name order and `order` lists the names in the order they were selected. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. The standard is `node --test test/*.test.js` passing in the workspace root.
